subject: Traffic-light release status + mitigation asks (QBR prep)
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Product Leads <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Eng Leads <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Release Managers <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Traffic-light release status + mitigation asks (QBR prep)

Team — attaching the traffic-light snapshot and a short set of mitigation asks so we can lock the QBR release narrative. High level: I want clear decisions by EOD tomorrow (05/04) on the red/yellow items so the exec deck can be finalized.

Snapshot (high level):
- Async batching v2: YELLOW — regression on 99p latency observed in internal perf run (see traffic_light_snapshot_20270503.csv).
- Model rollout (quantized variant): RED — reproducer shows token-level divergence and occasional NaN in KV cache (attached: quant-bug-trace.log).
- VPC gateway + docs: GREEN — infra is healthy but docs and runbook incomplete.
- SDK 2.3.0: YELLOW — packaging regression for Windows builds (low priority but visible).

Mitigation asks / decisions needed:
1) Quantization: do we (A) delay quantized canary and roll fp16 for initial canary, or (B) push urgent engineering fix and keep canary on schedule? Need a firm call and owner.
2) Async batching perf: assign 2 engineers to triage kernel mismatch and provide a short-term config that disables the hot-path optimization if needed.
3) Docs & runbook: Laura, confirm completion date and whether we can ship runbook as part of canary.
4) Canary date: propose moving canary from 05/05 to 05/07 if we choose (A) above; otherwise keep 05/05 but expect degraded confidence in quantized telemetry.

Attachments: traffic_light_snapshot_20270503.csv, mitigation_reqs_20270503.xlsx

Priority deadlines: decision on quantization by 09:00 PT 05/04. Triage update for async batching by EOD 05/04.

Thanks — will include the final decisions in the QBR slides.

Sean Gallagher
Head of Operations, Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
---
Note: please keep external partners looped only on the canary schedule once we have a clear decision.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>
Cc: Product Team <product@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 10:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Traffic-light release status + mitigation asks (QBR prep)

Sean — thanks for the crisp summary. Quick updates from product/CS side:
- Async batching: we can spare Laura and Rohan for a focused investigation. Hypothesis is a kernel-selection mismatch when sequence length distribution skews; we'll run targeted smoke load tests across the same sample traffic that failed. Plan: run tests tonight and report results tomorrow morning. Attached is the load-test-plan.md with test vectors.
- Quantization: from a product-risk perspective, rolling back to fp16 for the first canary is an acceptable fallback if engineering recommends it. We prefer to avoid a late hotfix unless we're confident in a fix window.

I will update the QBR slide to reflect the traffic-light and include both options so execs can see tradeoffs.

Marissa Cole
VP Product
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Traffic-light release status + mitigation asks (QBR prep)

Folks — quick technical readout from the infra team after reproducing the quantized-run locally:
- Bug root cause: quantized kernel invokes a reduced-precision path that doesn't initialize an internal accumulator under a rare tokenization border case; this produces NaN after about ~2k tokens in a deterministic repro.
- Repro steps and logs are in quant-bug-trace.log.

Options:
A) Skip quantized variant for initial canary and use fp16 model (low effort, immediate).
B) Apply a limited hotfix patch (adds defensive init) and run an extended regression; ETA for patch + regression ≈ 36–48h.
C) If we must keep quantization, we need to allocate 2 on-call engineers for real-time triage during the canary and accept a higher risk posture.

My recommendation: choose (A) for canary to preserve schedule and confidence; target a follow-up canary for quantized variant once the patch and a short regression run completes. I can own the patch if we decide (B).

Karthik Iyer
Director, Serving Infrastructure
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

- Canary date: moved to 05/07 to allow regression + docs handoff (owner: Laura).

- Runbooks & docs: Laura to complete by 05/05 12:00 PT; Marissa will update QBR deck.

Action items:
- Karthik: produce patch plan and ETA for quantized variant (target patch within 48h).
- Laura: finalize runbook and confirm gating checklist by 05/05 noon.
- Rohan & Laura: load-test results and perf triage report by EOD 05/04.

I'll notify Acme ops later tonight with the revised canary schedule once we have the smoke test result.
